types.desc: Property nvlists on their way from the command line to the kernel, property values read or stored (props ZAP, master node, zvol size ZAP).

types.name: Transaction
types.desc: A sync task joining the open txg, or a txg being synced.

types.name: Block pointer
types.desc: The new object set's root block pointer.

types.name: Control
types.desc: Calls that carry no payload: checks, object creation, accounting, mounts. Drawn dashed.

contexts.name: Kernel, in the thread of the calling process (an ioctl on /dev/zfs, mount(2) or umount(2)) or a helper thread it starts, outside syncing context and outside any dmu_tx
Open context: the calling thread, inside a dmu_tx
Syncing context: txg_sync thread or dp_sync_taskq workers, one txg at a time (sync tasks run here)
A dedicated kernel thread or zthr (here also the spa_zvol_taskq thread)
Runs in whichever context calls it

nodes.title: Administrator
nodes.role: The person or script typing the command. Every path in this graph that a command starts begins with a wire from this node; the arrows that come back into a command node are its results, errors and refusals.

nodes.title: zfs(8) command
nodes.role: The administrator's entry points this graph follows. `zfs create`: `-o prop=value` (repeatable, kept as strings), `-V size` makes a volume, `-b` sets its volblocksize, `-s` makes it sparse, `-p` creates missing parents (`-pp` creates them with canmount=off), `-u` skips the mount, `-n` only checks. `zfs clone snap fs` takes `-o`, `-p` and `-u` the same way. After a successful create or clone it mounts and shares a file system with canmount=on; a failure there only prints a warning and the dataset stays.

nodes.title: Volume defaults (-V, -b, -s)
nodes.role: Volume sizing done in userspace. volblocksize defaults to 16K, or to the largest power of 2 that fits in the pool's minimum allocation size when that is 32K or more (wide dRAID stripes, large sectors); a smaller `-b` only prints a warning. volsize is rounded up to a multiple of volblocksize. Unless `-s` or an explicit value, `zfs create` adds refreservation (reservation on pools older than version 9) of zvol_volsize_to_reservation(): volsize, scaled up when the least space-efficient raidz or dRAID top-level vdev stores the volume's blocks less efficiently than 128K blocks, times copies, plus room for the meta-dnode and every indirect block. refreservation=auto computes the same value.

nodes.title: libzfs mount / unmount

ref.code: do_mount(zfs_handle_t *zhp, const char *mntpt, const char *opts, int flags)

nodes.role: Mounting from userspace. zfs_is_mountable(): no mount for mountpoint=none or legacy, canmount=off, a zoned dataset in the global zone, or a redacted one. zfs_mount_at(): read-only if the pool is, encryption key check (encryption graph), mountpoint directory created if missing, a non-empty directory refused unless overlay=on (the default), then do_mount() calls mount(2). zfs_share() shares through libshare when sharenfs or sharesmb is set.

nodes.title: libzfs zfs_create() / zfs_clone()
nodes.role: Client-side checks before the ioctl. zfs_create(): the name must be valid and not too deeply nested, the pool and the parent must exist and the parent must be a file system (check_parents(), which also reads the parent's zoned property), and the dataset must not exist yet. The properties are validated; for a volume refreservation=auto is replaced by its computed size, and volsize must be present, nonzero and a multiple of volblocksize. zfs_crypto_create() adds encryption parameters if any, then lzc_create(). With `-p`, zfs_create_ancestors_props() first creates each missing ancestor as a file system and mounts it. zfs_clone() does the same checks for a clone and calls lzc_clone().

nodes.title: libzfs property validation
nodes.role: Turns the strings from the command line into a typed nvlist and rejects what the kernel would reject. Each name must be a known property that applies to this dataset type, a user property (a name with a colon) or a userquota@ style name. Read-only properties are refused, except set-once ones on a new dataset (normalization, utf8only, casesensitivity, volblocksize) and encryption key parameters. Values are parsed (sizes such as 10G, on and off, names such as lz4). recordsize and volblocksize must be a power of 2 from 512 bytes to the pool's maxblocksize; mountpoint must be an absolute path, none or legacy; sharenfs and sharesmb options are checked; normalization without utf8only adds utf8only=on, and normalization with utf8only=off is an error.

nodes.title: libzfs_core

ref.code: lzc_create(const char *fsname, enum lzc_dataset_type type, nvlist_t *props,

nodes.role: The thin ioctl layer. lzc_create() packs {type, props} and, for a new encryption root, the wrapping key in hidden_args; lzc_clone() packs {origin, props}; lzc_ioctl() sends the request to /dev/zfs.

nodes.title: Create and key ioctls
nodes.role: Kernel entry for ZFS_IOC_CREATE and ZFS_IOC_CLONE (the encryption graph shows the same handlers carrying wrapping keys). zfsdev_ioctl_common() checks the nvlist keys and the permission policy: create and mount permission on the parent, plus clone permission on the origin for a clone. zfs_ioc_create() refuses names with @ or %, fills the ZPL create-time properties or checks the volume size, builds the crypto parameters, runs dmu_objset_create(), and only then sets the remaining properties; a property failure destroys the new dataset again. A successful call is logged to the pool history.

nodes.title: ZPL create-time properties
nodes.role: File systems only. These are not DSL properties: zfs_fill_zplprops() takes version, normalization, utf8only, casesensitivity and the default user, group and project quotas out of the property list and puts them in zplprops for the new master node. Values not given are copied now from the parent's master node (or the default), so they are inherited once, at create time. A ZPL version above what the pool version allows, or one of these properties on a pre-normalization version, is refused with ENOTSUP. normalization forces utf8only on. casesensitivity=insensitive marks the dataset DS_FLAG_CI_DATASET.

nodes.title: Volume checks
nodes.role: Kernel checks for a new volume, before anything is created: volsize must be in the property list; volblocksize (default 16K) must be a power of 2 from 512 bytes to 16M, and above 128K needs the large_blocks feature and must not exceed zfs_max_recordsize; volsize must be a nonzero multiple of volblocksize.

nodes.title: dsl_crypto_params
nodes.role: Every create builds crypto parameters, with command DCP_CMD_NONE. encryption, keyformat, pbkdf2salt and pbkdf2iters are taken out of the property list here, so they never become ordinary DSL properties; without them the parameters mean "inherit from the parent". What happens with a key is in the encryption graph.

nodes.title: zfs_set_prop_nvlist()
nodes.role: Applies the `-o` properties still in the list after the create (not volsize, volblocksize, the ZPL create-time ones or the encryption parameters). Best effort: each value's type is checked, zfs_check_settable() checks pool version and features (for example a recordsize above 128K needs large_blocks and must not exceed zfs_max_recordsize) and the set permission, and zfs_prop_set_special() hands quota, reservation, refquota, refreservation, volmode, snapdev and a few others to their own handlers (the first four are sync tasks of their own). Everything else is set in one batch. The last error is returned.

nodes.title: dmu_objset_create() / dsl_dataset_clone()

ref.code: dmu_objset_create(const char *name, dmu_objset_type_t type, uint64_t flags,

nodes.role: Open-context wrappers that turn a create or clone request into one DSL sync task (6 blocks of MOS space, normal space check). When the task has synced they call zvol_create_minors() for the new name, so a new volume gets its block device before zfs_ioc_create() sets the remaining properties.

nodes.title: dsl_sync_task()
nodes.role: Runs a metadata change in syncing context. The check function runs once in the calling thread as a quick test, the task is queued on the open txg, and the caller waits until that txg has synced. In syncing context dsl_sync_task_sync() checks pool space, re-runs the check with the pool config lock held as writer, and then calls the sync function. The create and each later property change are separate sync tasks, each with its own txg wait.

nodes.title: dmu_tx (transaction)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Here a transaction on the MOS directory only pins the sync task to the currently open txg.

nodes.title: TXG: syncing (txg_sync_thread)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Syncs the txg the create task joined. txg_wait_synced() is why `zfs create` returns only when the new dataset is on disk.

nodes.title: spa_sync()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Writes one txg in passes until the MOS stays clean. A new dataset needs at least two: sync tasks run only in pass 1, and the objects they create are written in pass 2.

nodes.title: dsl_pool_sync()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Order within a pass: the dirty datasets are written, their space deltas applied (dsl_dataset_sync_done()), the dirty DSL directories synced, the MOS written, and only then (in pass 1) the queued sync tasks run. The create task therefore dirties the MOS and the new dataset again, and the next pass writes them.

nodes.title: dmu_objset_sync()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Writes the new object set: its dirty dnodes (master node, root directory, SA registry and unlinked set, or the zvol objects), then the meta-dnode and the objset block. When the objset block's address is known it is copied into ds_bp of the dataset object; the MOS's own objset block address goes to the uberblock.

nodes.title: dmu_objset_create_check() / _sync()
nodes.role: The create sync task. Check: no @ in the name, name length and nesting depth (ENAMETOOLONG), the parent directory exists and the name does not (EEXIST), the encryption parameters fit the parent, filesystem_limit on the parent and its ancestors is not exceeded (EDQUOT), and the parent is a file system, not a volume (ZFS_ERR_WRONG_PARENT). Sync: creates the DSL objects, the object set and the type's first objects, and records "create" in the pool history. For an encrypted dataset it also writes the new object set at once, inside the task, while the key mapping is still held.

nodes.title: dsl_dataset_clone_check() / _sync()
nodes.role: The clone sync task. Check: as for create (name, parent, EEXIST, filesystem_limit), and the origin must be a snapshot (EINVAL). Sync: dsl_dataset_create_sync() with the snapshot as origin, then a "clone" history record. No object set is created and no type init runs: the clone's tree is the snapshot's, including its master node or zvol objects, so its create-time properties are the origin's. A non-empty ZIL header inherited from the origin is zeroed (dsl_dataset_zero_zil()), which writes the clone's object set at once.

nodes.title: dsl_dataset_create_sync()
nodes.role: Creates the DSL directory first, then the head dataset object: random guid, fsid, creation time and txg, an empty snapshot-names ZAP and a deadlist. Its origin is the given snapshot for a clone, otherwise the pool's $ORIGIN@$ORIGIN, whose empty block pointer becomes ds_bp. Encryption is handed to dsl_dataset_create_crypt_sync(). The directory's head-dataset pointer is set, the creator gets the create-time permissions delegated on its ancestors (`zfs allow -c`), and with the filesystem and snapshot limit feature active the new directory starts with zero counts.

nodes.title: dsl_dir_create_sync()
nodes.role: Allocates the new DSL directory object in the MOS, enters its name in the parent's child-directory ZAP, sets the parent pointer and creates its own empty props ZAP and child-directory ZAP. Where filesystem limits are tracked, the filesystem_count of every ancestor goes up by one. Nothing is copied from the parent: inherited properties are looked up at read time.

nodes.title: DSL directory tree (MOS)
nodes.role: Where datasets live: objects in the pool's meta-object set (MOS). The MOS object directory names the root DSL directory (root_dataset), which dsl_pool_create() made together with the hidden $MOS, $FREE and $ORIGIN directories and the pool's root file system. Each DSL directory has a child-directory ZAP (name to object number), a props ZAP, quota, reservation and used counters, and points at its head DSL dataset, whose ds_bp is the root block pointer of the dataset's object set. dsl_dir_hold() resolves pool/a/b by walking the child-directory ZAPs. $ORIGIN@$ORIGIN (pool version 11 and later) is an empty snapshot that every new file system and volume formally descends from; dsl_dir_is_clone() does not count that as a clone.

nodes.title: Encrypted dataset creation
nodes.role: Called for every new dataset. Check (inside the create check): an unencrypted dataset may carry no key parameters; an encrypted one needs the encryption feature and either a complete new key or a parent whose key is loaded. Sync: a clone of an encrypted snapshot shares its origin's DSL Crypto Key, a dataset whose effective encryption is off returns at once, and any other gets a master key of its own. The encryption graph follows this branch.

nodes.title: dmu_objset_create_impl()
nodes.role: Turns the empty block pointer into a live object set: opens it from the dataset (a hole, so nothing is read), allocates the meta-dnode (16K blocks of dnodes, 128K indirect blocks) with enough levels for every possible object, so that it never has to gain a level later, sets os_type to ZFS or ZVOL, and marks user, group and project accounting complete when those features are enabled. dsl_dataset_dirty() queues the dataset to be written in this txg. The MOS itself was made by the same function at pool creation.

nodes.title: ZPL init: master node and root directory
nodes.role: What makes an object set a file system. zfs_create_fs() claims object 1 as the master node ZAP and stores the zplprops in it (normalization, utf8only, casesensitivity, default quotas) and the ZPL version (the requested one if lower than the pool allows). With ZPL version 5 (system attributes) it creates the SA attribute registry; it always creates the unlinked set (files removed while still open) and, with zfs_mknode(), the root directory: mode 0755, owned by the uid and gid of the creating process. Their object numbers go into the master node. dsl_pool_create() runs zfs_create_fs() for the pool's root file system too.

nodes.title: zvol_create_cb()
nodes.role: What makes an object set a volume: object 1 (DMU_OT_ZVOL) holds the data, with volblocksize as its block size, and object 2 is a ZAP whose "size" entry is volsize. Both values are removed from the property list here, so they are never stored as DSL properties; `zfs get` reads them back from these objects. No data block is written: the volume is all holes until written.

nodes.title: dnode (object)

ref.code: dnode_allocate(dnode_t *dn, dmu_object_type_t ot, int blocksize, int ibs,

nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Every object the create makes is a dnode allocated in syncing context: dmu_object_alloc() and its variants (also used by zap_create()) for the new MOS objects (DSL directory, DSL dataset, their ZAPs), dmu_object_claim() and zap_create_claim() for the fixed object numbers inside the new object set (master node, zvol objects), and dnode_allocate() directly for the meta-dnode. dnode_allocate() calls dnode_setdirty(), which puts the dnode on its object set's dirty list for this txg and dirties the dataset.

nodes.title: dsl_props_set()
nodes.role: Sets a batch of ordinary properties all-or-nothing, as one sync task (space for 2 blocks per property, reserved-space check). Check: name and string value lengths. Sync: for a local value dsl_prop_set_sync_impl() writes propname into the props ZAP and removes any propname$inherit entry; integer properties are pushed to the callbacks of open datasets that inherit them; each change is recorded in the pool history.

nodes.title: quota / reservation (dsl_dir)

ref.code: dsl_dir_set_quota(const char *ddname, zprop_source_t source, uint64_t quota)

nodes.role: Space limits of a DSL directory: they cover the dataset, its snapshots and all its descendants. Each is its own sync task with the extra-reserved space check. quota: a new quota below the reservation or below the space already used plus pending writes fails with ENOSPC. reservation: checked only in syncing context; its growth must fit in what the parent can still provide and stay within the quota (ENOSPC). The value goes to the props ZAP and to dd_quota or dd_reserved. The part of a reservation above the space used is charged to the parent as reserved child space (part of usedbychildren), and from there up the tree, so siblings see less available space.

nodes.title: refquota / refreservation (dsl_dataset)
nodes.role: Limits of the head dataset alone, not its snapshots or descendants. refquota: refused below the bytes the dataset already references or below its refreservation (ENOSPC); cached as ds_quota. refreservation: checked in syncing context; the part not already covered by the dataset's unique bytes must fit in the space available to its directory and must not exceed refquota (ENOSPC). That part is charged at once as usedbyrefreservation (DD_USED_REFRSRV), which counts in the used of every ancestor; later writes are absorbed by it instead of growing the parents' used. For a thick volume this is how its whole size is set aside at create time.

nodes.title: DSL props ZAP and inheritance
nodes.role: Each DSL directory's props ZAP holds only what was set on it: propname for a local value, propname$recvd for a received one, propname$inherit for an explicit inherit over a received value. A new dataset's ZAP starts empty, so every property it did not get with `-o` is inherited. Reading a value (dsl_prop_get_dd()) looks in this directory, then in each parent up to the root, and falls back to the default; where it was found is the source `zfs get` shows. Non-inheritable properties are looked up in this directory only. dsl_prop_register() reads a value and keeps a callback; when a value is set on an ancestor, dsl_prop_changed_notify() walks the child directories, skips any subtree that sets the property itself, and calls the callbacks.

nodes.title: dsl_dir space accounting
nodes.role: Each DSL directory tracks its used bytes (broken down into head, snapshots, children, refreservation and child reservations), its quota and its reservation. Changes are applied in syncing context and rolled up into every ancestor, adjusted so that space inside a reservation is not counted twice. dsl_dir_space_available() is what a check sees: the smaller of what the parent can provide (plus this directory's unused reservation) and the room left under its own quota, capped by the pool size at the root. A new dataset starts with only its first metadata blocks charged.

nodes.title: zpl mount (zfs_domount)
nodes.role: Kernel side of mount(2) on Linux. zpl_get_tree() holds the dataset and finds or creates the superblock; zfs_domount() creates the zfsvfs, which owns the object set (zfsvfs_create()) and reads the master node (zfsvfs_init()); the superblock block size is recordsize. zfsvfs_setup() registers the property callbacks, opens the ZIL, drains the unlinked set and replays any intent log (there is none on a new file system); zfs_root() then gets the root directory inode. An encrypted dataset needs its key here (encryption graph).

nodes.title: zvol device node

ref.code: zvol_alloc(dev_t dev, const char *name, uint64_t dsobj, uint64_t volsize,

nodes.role: Creates block devices for volumes on the spa_zvol_taskq while the caller waits. zvol_create_minors_impl() searches the name and its children for volumes and, with snapdev=visible, their snapshots. On Linux zvol_os_create_minor() owns the volume, reads its size and block size, allocates the zvol state and gendisk, replays its ZIL and adds the disk, which appears as /dev/zdN (16 minors per volume, for partitions); the udev rule 60-zvol.rules adds the /dev/zvol/pool/name link. volmode=none, or the zvol_inhibit_dev tunable, means no device. This runs before zfs_ioc_create() sets the `-o` properties, so a volmode or snapdev given at create is applied afterwards by its own handler.

a special property that failed is retried once after the others (retrynvl); all ordinary ones are set in one batch: dsl_props_set(name, local, genericnvl)

dsl_sync_task() -> dsl_props_set_sync_impl() -> dsl_prop_set_sync_impl(): in dd_props_zapobj any propname$inherit entry is removed and propname is set with zap_update(); dsl_prop_changed_notify() for integer properties

quota below dd_used_bytes plus pending writes or below the reservation: ENOSPC; reservation growth beyond dsl_dir_space_available() of the parent or above quota: ENOSPC; in sync the reservation above used is charged to the parent as DD_USED_CHILD_RSRV
dsl_prop_set_sync_impl() stores the value in the props ZAP; dd_quota or dsl_dir_set_reservation_sync_impl() updates the directory

refreservation: the part not covered by unique bytes must fit in dsl_dir_space_available() (ENOSPC otherwise); in sync ds_reserved is set and that part is charged as DD_USED_REFRSRV, rolled up by dsl_dir_diduse_transfer_space_impl()
refquota below ds_referenced_bytes or below refreservation is refused; in sync it is stored and cached as ds_quota; refreservation is stored with dsl_prop_set_sync_impl()
unless -u: zfs_mount_and_share(); a ZFS_TYPE_VOLUME is skipped; with ZFS_CANMOUNT_ON zfs_mount() then zfs_share(); failures only warn

zfs_is_mountable() reads ZFS_PROP_MOUNTPOINT from the values ZFS_IOC_OBJSET_STATS returned (dsl_prop_get_all() with sources); an inherited mountpoint gets the path below the source dataset appended (relpath); none, ZFS_MOUNTPOINT_LEGACY or ZFS_CANMOUNT_OFF means no mount

zfs_mount_at(): mkdirp() of the mountpoint (0755), ZFS_PROP_OVERLAY decides whether a non-empty directory (dir_is_empty()) is refused; do_mount() -> mount(2) type MNTTYPE_ZFS; in the kernel zpl_get_tree() -> zfs_domount()

zfsvfs_create() -> dmu_objset_own(); zfsvfs_init() reads the master node: ZFS_PROP_VERSION (ENOTSUP if newer than the pool allows), normalization, utf8only, casesensitivity, ZFS_ROOT_OBJ and the unlinked set

refs.code: error = dmu_objset_own(osname, DMU_OST_ZFS, ro, B_TRUE, zfsvfs, &os);

wires.label: dsl_prop_get_integer() for recordsize (superblock block size); zfsvfs_setup() -> zfs_register_callbacks(): dsl_prop_register() for atime, recordsize (blksz_changed_cb), readonly, xattr and others reads each value via dsl_prop_get_int_ds() and calls its callback now and on every later change
-p: makeprops_parents() (-pp: ZFS_PROP_CANMOUNT off for the ancestors); an existing target makes zfs create -p succeed at once (zfs_dataset_exists()); zfs_create_ancestors_props()
check_parents() finds the deepest existing ancestor; create_parents() then, for each missing one in turn, zfs_create(), zfs_mount() (nothing with canmount=off) and zfs_share()
zfs clone snap fs: zfs_do_clone() opens the ZFS_TYPE_SNAPSHOT (with -p, zfs_create_ancestors_props() first) and calls zfs_clone()
zfs_clone(): check_parents(), zfs_valid_proplist() for the origin's type, zfs_crypto_clone_check(), then lzc_clone(name, origin, props)

zfs_ioc_clone() -> dsl_dataset_clone(name, origin): no ZPL or volume properties are filled in and no type callback is passed
dsl_sync_task_sync(): dst_checkfunc dsl_dataset_clone_check() (filesystem_limit with dsl_fs_ss_limit_check(), origin must be a snapshot: ds_is_snapshot), then dst_syncfunc dsl_dataset_clone_sync()
dsl_dataset_create_sync(parent directory, last component, origin snapshot)

clone: ds_bp and referenced bytes copied from the origin snapshot (no block is copied); origin's ds_num_children incremented, clone added to its ds_next_clones_obj; dd_origin_obj set; DD_FIELD_LIVELIST added when enabled; dsl_dataset_zero_zil()

paths.title: Create a file system (zfs create pool/fs)
paths.summary: `zfs create -o compression=lz4 tank/home`: from the command line through one sync task that adds the DSL directory, the DSL dataset and a new object set with a master node and root directory, to the property batch and the mount.
paths.ends: tank/home exists on disk with an empty root directory owned by the creating user; its props ZAP holds only compression; everything else is inherited from tank. For an encrypted file system the key part is `zfs-encryption-keys:create`.

options.label: Unencrypted (dsl_dataset_create_crypt_sync() returns at once, no steps of its own)
Encrypted, given encryption=on or an encrypted parent

steps.note: a new master key, or the parent's encryption root wraps it: path zfs-encryption-keys:create
compression has a special handler, but it needs a sync task only for zstd (to activate the feature); lz4 joins the batch
continue with path mount

paths.title: Create a volume (zfs create -V)
paths.summary: `zfs create -V 10G tank/vol`: userspace picks the block size and, unless `-s`, a refreservation; the kernel checks the sizes, creates an object set holding the volume's data object and size ZAP, makes the block device, and only then sets the refreservation.
paths.ends: /dev/zdN and /dev/zvol/tank/vol exist; the volume is all holes. A thick volume has its full size set aside in the space accounting of every ancestor; a sparse one uses space only as it is written. I/O to the device follows `zfs-io-flow:zvol_write`.

options.label: Default: refreservation of the full size plus metadata

steps.note: -s: no refreservation is added; only volsize and volblocksize go on
zfs_create() validates the list again
the whole reservation is charged to tank and every ancestor now; ENOSPC here removes the new volume (path quota_resv)
a volume is not mounted

paths.title: zfs create -p: missing parents first
paths.summary: `zfs create -p tank/a/b/c` when only tank exists. Each missing ancestor is a complete create of its own (path create_fs), with its own ioctl and txg, followed by a mount; the operation as a whole is not atomic.
paths.ends: tank/a, tank/a/b and tank/a/b/c exist. If a later step fails, the ancestors already created stay. With -pp the ancestors exist only as containers for properties and children.

options.label: -p: ancestors are ordinary file systems and are mounted
-pp: ancestors get canmount=off and are not mounted

steps.note: zfs_create() for the first missing ancestor, tank/a
one complete create per missing ancestor, as in path create_fs
canmount=off is the only property of each ancestor
then the target tank/a/b/c itself, as in path create_fs, with the -o properties

paths.title: Where each -o property goes
paths.summary: `zfs create -o casesensitivity=insensitive -o quota=10G -o refreservation=1G -o atime=off tank/share`: the same command line ends up in four different places, at different times.
paths.ends: casesensitivity is in the master node and can never change; quota is in the props ZAP and dd_quota; refreservation in the props ZAP and ds_reserved; atime in the props ZAP. If any of them failed, the dataset no longer exists and `zfs create` reports the error.

options.label: One property fails (for example quota below the reservation): the new dataset is destroyed

steps.note: casesensitivity leaves the list here
and is written into the new master node by the create task
encryption parameters would leave the list here
the create itself runs as in path create_fs
quota, refreservation and atime are still in the list

paths.title: Inherited values: copied once, or looked up for ever
paths.summary: What a new tank/home/alice has for properties it was not given: the ZPL create-time ones are copied from tank/home's master node at create; every other property is found at read time by walking up the DSL directories.
paths.ends: `zfs get` shows inherited properties with the ancestor as their source. A later `zfs set atime=off tank/home` changes nothing in alice's ZAP but reaches the mounted alice through dsl_prop_changed_notify(); a later change of normalization on tank/home is impossible, and alice keeps her copy.

steps.note: normalization, utf8only, casesensitivity copied from tank/home's master node
only the -o properties are stored; the new props ZAP is otherwise empty
mountpoint: tank/home has /home, so alice mounts at /home/alice
recordsize, atime and the others are found on tank/home or tank, or are defaults

paths.title: Quota and reservation checks at create
paths.summary: `-o quota=`, `-o reservation=`, `-o refquota=` or `-o refreservation=` at create (refreservation also the automatic one of a thick volume). Each is its own sync task after the dataset exists, checked against what the parent can still provide.
paths.ends: with the space available, the reservation is charged to the parent (reservation) or to the dataset's own usedbyrefreservation and its ancestors (refreservation), and siblings see that much less available space. Without it, `zfs create` fails with "out of space" and the dataset is gone again (its destroy: `zfs-snapshot-lifecycle:destroy_filesystem`).

options.label: quota and reservation (DSL directory, includes descendants and snapshots)
ENOSPC: the new dataset is destroyed

paths.title: The sync task and the txg that writes the new dataset
paths.summary: The create as the txg sees it: the task joins the open txg, runs in sync pass 1 after the MOS has been written, and dirties the MOS and the new dataset, which pass 2 writes.
paths.ends: the new DSL objects and object set are on disk once the uberblock of this txg is written (`zfs-io-flow:txg_sync`); txg_wait_synced() returns and `zfs create` continues with the properties.

steps.note: pass 1
pass 2: the new dataset is now on dp_dirty_datasets

paths.title: Mount after create
paths.summary: `zfs create` mounts a new file system with canmount=on itself (unless `-u`); `zfs mount` takes the same route.
paths.ends: the file system is mounted at its mountpoint and shared if sharenfs or sharesmb is set; writes go through `zfs-io-flow:write_async`. An encrypted file system needs its key loaded: `zfs-encryption-keys:mount`.

options.label: canmount=on and a mountpoint path: mounted
canmount=off or noauto, or mountpoint=none or legacy: not mounted

paths.title: Clone from a snapshot (zfs clone)
paths.summary: `zfs clone tank/home@monday tank/test`: a new DSL directory and head dataset whose ds_bp is the snapshot's, so it shares every block and copies nothing; no object set or type init is created.
paths.ends: tank/test references the same blocks as tank/home@monday and uses no space until it diverges; the snapshot cannot be destroyed while the clone exists. How later writes and the clone's destroy are accounted is in the snapshot graph (`zfs-snapshot-lifecycle:destroy_filesystem`).

options.label: Unencrypted origin (no steps of its own)
Encrypted origin: the clone shares its DSL Crypto Key

model: A dataset is a set of objects in the pool's meta-object set (MOS): a DSL directory (its name in the parent's child-directory ZAP, its own props ZAP, quota, reservation and space counters) and a head DSL dataset (guid, creation txg, snapshot names, deadlist, and ds_bp, the root of the dataset's object set). The pool's root file system was created the same way at pool creation, beside the hidden $MOS, $FREE and $ORIGIN directories.

`zfs create` is several separate steps, not one transaction. libzfs validates names and properties and computes volume defaults; one ioctl creates the dataset in one sync task; then the remaining `-o` properties are set by further sync tasks, and if one of them fails the new dataset is destroyed again. Mounting and sharing happen afterwards in userspace, and their failure does not undo the create.

The create sync task runs in syncing context, in sync pass 1 of a txg, after that pass has written the MOS. It allocates the DSL objects, an empty object set with its meta-dnode, and runs the type's init: for a file system the master node, SA registry, unlinked set and root directory; for a volume its data object and size ZAP. The next sync pass writes all of it, the uberblock commits it, and only then does `zfs create` return.

Properties live in different places. Ordinary properties go into the new directory's props ZAP only when given with `-o`; inherited values are never copied, they are found at read time by walking up the parent directories, and a later change on an ancestor reaches mounted descendants through callbacks. The ZPL create-time properties (normalization, utf8only, casesensitivity, version) are copied from the parent's master node into the new master node and can never change. volsize and volblocksize live in the volume's own objects, the encryption parameters in its DSL Crypto Key.

quota and reservation belong to the DSL directory and cover descendants and snapshots; refquota and refreservation belong to the head dataset. A volume created without `-s` gets a refreservation of its size plus metadata, computed in userspace; setting it charges every ancestor at once, and an ENOSPC there makes `zfs create` fail and remove the new volume.

A file system appears in the namespace only when libzfs mounts it: mountpoint inherited as the parent's path plus the name, directory created, mount(2), and zfs_domount() reads the master node and registers property callbacks. A volume appears as /dev/zdN when the zvol taskq creates its block device, unless volmode=none.

A clone is a create whose dataset starts from a snapshot's block pointer: nothing is copied and no type init runs. Even a plain create is formally a clone of the hidden empty snapshot $ORIGIN@$ORIGIN.
simplifications: A sync task's check function runs twice, once in the calling thread and once in syncing context; the diagram draws the check where its effect matters, once, in syncing context.

Each property set after the create (quota, reservation, refquota, refreservation and the batch of ordinary properties) is its own sync task with its own dmu_tx and txg wait, exactly like the create task; the diagram draws these as direct wires from zfs_set_prop_nvlist() to their check and sync nodes.
With `-p`, every missing ancestor goes through the whole create path; the path draws that repetition once.
The txg is drawn down to dmu_objset_sync(); the zio pipeline, block allocation and the uberblock write are in the I/O graph.

Encryption at create is one branch; the key handling is in the encryption graph. Delegated permissions, zones and user namespaces, dry runs, user and project quotas and the pool history are mentioned in node text only.

The DSL directory tree is one node standing for the on-disk objects (MOS object directory, DSL directories and datasets, their ZAPs); the pool's own creation of the root dataset and $ORIGIN is described in it, not drawn.
Returns are drawn only where a result or an error changes the outcome (a failed property destroying the dataset).

page.title: ZFS Dataset Creation
page.intro: This spec describes a diagram of what `zfs create` (a file system or a volume) and `zfs clone` actually do: where a new dataset sits in the pool's structure (the MOS, the tree of DSL directories, DSL datasets and their object sets), how libzfs and the kernel validate the properties, which properties are copied at create time and which are only looked up through inheritance, how quota, reservation and refreservation are checked and accounted, which txg writes the new dataset to disk, and what happens afterwards when a file system is mounted or a volume gets its block device.
